Page iii
Introduction
This
document
specifies
the
TMF674
REST
API
for
Geographic
Site
Management.
A
Geographic
Site
is
a
specialization
of
the
abstract
Place
entity,
alongside
GeographicAddress
and
GeographicLocation
.
A Geographic Site represents a
managed
location, such as a retail store, warehouse or data
centre.
It
will
typically
have
associations
with
a
collection
of
relatedParty
that
are
in
roles
of
responsibility
for
the
Site.
A
large
site
might
be
described
in
terms
of
multiple
relevant
addresses
and/or
locations,
both
distinguished
by
role
(such
as
a
delivery-
address
, or
office-entrance
).
A Geographic Site can manage various unstructured site features, ranging from survey data
to safety guidelines and hazard information.
This API is closely related to two other APIs that also cover the SID GeographicPlace entity:
•
Geographic
Address
—
manages
places
defined
in
a
structured
textual
way
(e.g.,
street name, street number) and validates the existence of a given address.
•
Geographic Location
— manages places defined as geometric objects in a spatial
reference system (coordinates, boundaries).
Supported Operations
The Geographic Site API supports the following operations:
•
Create
a new site
•
Partially update
an existing site
•
Retrieve
a list of sites, filtered by given criteria
•
Retrieve
a specific site
•
Notify
events related to a geographic site, including:
◦
Site creation
◦
Site removal
◦
Site status change
◦
Site value change (any data update within a site)

Sample Use Cases
Below there are several use cases listed for the usage of the Geographic Site API.
Field Service Management for Engineering Services
Description
:
A
telecommunication
company
providing
fixed
fiber
broadband
services
needs
to
efficiently
manage
field
service
operations
for
installation,
maintenance,
and
repair of fiber optic infrastructure across various locations.
Maintenance and Routine Inspections
:
Description
: Regular maintenance and inspections are required to ensure the integrity and
functionality
of
the
fiber
optic
network.
The
system
schedules
routine
maintenance
inspections for fiber optic network sites.
Field service technicians receive notifications of scheduled maintenance tasks along with
site
details.
Technicians
use
the
Geographic
Site
API
to
retrieve
site
information.
Technicians visit each site, perform maintenance tasks, conduct inspections, and update
site
status
and
maintenance
records
accordingly.
Any
issues
or
anomalies
discovered
during inspections are documented and reported for further investigation or repair.
Hazard Identification and Mitigation
Description
:
Field
service
technicians
need
to
be
aware
of
potential
hazards
present
at
fiber optic network sites to ensure their safety and the integrity of the infrastructure.
Hazard
information
such
as
underground
utilities,
hazardous
materials,
or
environmental
risks is stored against geographic sites using the Geographic Site API. Before visiting a site
for
installation,
maintenance,
or
repair
tasks,
field
service
technicians
retrieve
hazard
information associated with the site. Technicians assess the potential risks and implement
necessary safety measures and precautions to mitigate hazards during site visits.
By
proactively
addressing
hazards,
the
company
reduces
the
likelihood
of
accidents,
injuries, and service disruptions, enhancing overall operational safety and efficiency.
Emergency Response Planning
Description
:
In
the
event
of
emergencies
such
as
natural
disasters
or
infrastructure
failures, field service teams need to quickly assess and respond to hazards affecting fiber
optic network sites.
Hazard
information
including
vulnerability
to
floods,
earthquakes,
or
power
outages
is
stored against geographic sites in the system. During emergency response planning, field
Geographic Site User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 2
service
managers
use
the
GeographicSite
API
to
identify
high-risk
sites
and
prioritize
mitigation
efforts.
Field
service
technicians
receive
updated
hazard
information
and
emergency response protocols for affected sites.
In
the
event
of
an
emergency,
technicians
can
quickly
assess
hazards,
prioritize
safety
measures, and coordinate with emergency responders to minimize service disruptions and
ensure the safety of personnel and infrastructure.
Regulatory Compliance and Reporting
Description
:
Telecommunication
companies
must
comply
with
regulatory
requirements
related
to
workplace
safety
and
environmental
protection,
including
the
management
of
hazardous materials and environmental risks.
Hazard information such as the presence of hazardous chemicals or protected habitats is
stored against geographic sites in compliance with regulatory standards. During regulatory
audits
or
inspections,
field
service
managers
use
the
GeographicSite
API
to
retrieve
comprehensive hazard data for reporting purposes.
Regulatory
compliance
reports
are
generated,
documenting
hazard
identification,
mitigation measures, and ongoing monitoring efforts at fiber optic network sites.
By
maintaining
accurate
hazard
records
and
demonstrating
proactive
risk
management
practices,
the
company
ensures
compliance
with
regulatory
requirements
and
mitigates
the risk of fines or penalties.
Franchise Management
Description
: A company with multiple franchise locations needs to efficiently manage and
track all their sites.
The GeographicSite API enables the company to create, update, and retrieve information
about
each
franchise
location.
They
can
easily
add
new
franchise
sites
as
the
business
expands, update site details such as operating hours or contact information, and retrieve
lists of sites for reporting or analysis purposes.
Further
examples
of
use
cases
are
available
in
TM
Forum
Open
Digital
Architecture
business scenarios and use cases (IG1228).

Support of polymorphism and extension
patterns
Support
for
polymorphic
collections,
types,
and
schema-based
extensions
is
provided
through
a
set
of
generic
meta-attributes
described
below.
Polymorphism
in
collections
occurs
when
entities
inherit
from
base
entities.
For
instance,
GeographicSite
,
GeographicAddress
,
and
GeographicLocation
inherit
properties
from
the
abstract
Place
entity.
Generic
support
for
polymorphism
and
pattern
extensions
is
detailed
in
the
TMF
API
Guidelines, Part 2 (TMF630).
The
@type
attribute represents the actual class type of an entity. For example, within a list
of
Place
instances,
some
may
be
instances
of
GeographicSite
while
others
could
be
instances
of
GeographicAddress
or
GeographicLocation
.
The
@type
attribute
provides
this
information.
All
resources
and
sub-resources
of
this
API
have
@type
attributes that can be provided when useful.
The
@referredType
attribute
can
be
used
within
reference
entities
(such
as
a
GeographicAddress
object)
to
explicitly
denote
the
actual
entity
type
of
the
referred
class.
Note
that
in
reference
entities,
the
@type
attribute,
when
used,
denotes
the
class
type of the reference itself, such as
AddressRef
, and not the class type of the referred
object.
However,
since
reference
classes
are
rarely
sub-classed,
@type
is
generally
not
useful in reference objects.
The
@schemaLocation
property
can
be
used
in
resources
to
specify
user-defined
properties of an entity or to specify the expected characteristics of an entity.
The
@baseType
attribute
explicitly
provides
the
base
class
of
a
given
resource
that
has
been extended.

CalendarPeriod sub-resource fields
The CalendarPeriod schema represents a period of time within a calendar, defining various
attributes such as the applicable day, timezone, hour period, and status. It is designed to
capture information about the availability or status of a calendar period, which can be used
in scheduling, booking, or resource allocation applications.
Geographic Site User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.

* mon

* fri
* sat
* sun
* weekdays
* weekend
hourPeriod
A HourPeriod [0..*]. Start and end time range in 24-hour
HH:mm format.
status
A String [1]. Indication of the availability of the calendar
period (e.g.: available, booked, etc.).
timeZone
A String. Indication of the timezone applicable to the
calendar information in ISO 8601 timezone: either 'Z' for
UTC or an offset like +02:00 or -05:30.

A String. The end of the hour period, expressed in 24-hour

startHour
A String. The beginning of the hour period, expressed in
24-hour HH:mm format (e.g., 09:00 for 9 AM, 17:30 for
5:30 PM).

ExternalIdentifier sub-resource fields
An identification of an entity that is owned by or originates in a software system different
from
the
current
system,
for
example
a
ProductOrder
handed
off
from
a
commerce
platform
into
an
order
handling
system.
The
structure
identifies
the
system
itself,
the
nature
of
the
entity
within
the
system
(e.g.
class
name)
and
the
unique
ID
of
the
entity
within the system. It is anticipated that multiple external IDs can be held for a single entity,
e.g. if the entity passed through multiple systems on the way to the current system. In this
case
the
consumer
is
expected
to
sequence
the
IDs
in
the
array
in
reverse
order
of
provenance, i.e. most recent system first in the list.
externalIdentifierType
A String. Type of the identification, typically would be the
type of the entity within the external system.
id
A String [1]. Identification of the entity within the external
system.
owner
A String. Name of the external system that owns the
entity.

Deletes a GeographicSite
DELETE /geographicSite/{id}?{filtering}
Description
This operation deletes a GeographicSite entity.
Usage samples
Here's an example of a request for delete a specific GeographicSite.
Request
DELETE /geographicSite/ae4b915f-16f5-4f05-a3c7-8c6a99c7d24b
Content-Type: application/json
Response
204
Geographic Site User Guide

Page 65
API NOTIFICATIONS
For
every
single
of
operation
on
the
entities
use
the
following
templates
and
provide
sample REST notification POST calls.
It is assumed that the Pub/Sub uses the Register and UnRegister mechanisms described in
the REST Guidelines reproduced below.
Register listener
POST /hub
Description
Sets
the
communication
endpoint
address
the
service
instance
must
use
to
deliver
information about its health state, execution state, failures and metrics. Subsequent POST
calls will be rejected by the service if it does not support multiple listeners. In this case
DELETE /api/hub/{id} must be called before an endpoint can be created again.
Behavior
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 204 if the request was successful.
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 409 if request is not successful.
Usage Samples

Description
Clears the communication endpoint address that was set by creating the Hub..
Behavior
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 204 if the request was successful.
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 404 if the resource is not found.
